title: Signed local basis powers and product normalization
statement: Let $(\mathcal C,J)$ be a site small relative to the coefficient universe, let $R$ be a commutative ring sheaf, and let $L$ be a sheaf of $R$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Use the signed powers $L^{[m]}$ of [def-pur-signed-line-scalar-normalization-data], the sheaf tensor of [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], and the internal sheaf Hom of [def-pur-sheaf-hom]. For $U\in\mathcal C$, define $\operatorname{SignedLineBasisPowers}(L,U,e)$ for sections $e_m\in L^{[m]}(U)$, $m\in\mathbf Z$, by the following conditions: for every $m$ and every arrow $V\to U$, the map $R(V)\to L^{[m]}(V)$ sending $r$ to $r e_m|_V$ is bijective; $e_0=1$; $e_{n+2}=e_{n+1}\otimes e_1$ for every $n\geq0$; and the functional $e_{-(n+1)}$ evaluated on $e_{n+1}|_V$ is $1\in R(V)$ for every $n\geq0$ and every $V\to U$. For a family of isomorphisms $\mu_{a,b}:L^{[a]}\otimes_R L^{[b]}\xrightarrow\sim L^{[a+b]}$, define $\operatorname{SignedLineProductNormalized}(L,\mu)$ to mean that $\mu_{a,b}(e_a\otimes e_b)=e_{a+b}$ for every $U$, every family $e$ satisfying this signed-basis predicate, and all integers $a,b$. These are predicates; they do not assert existence of a signed basis or of a normalized product.
